design.summary:
34 of the 38 FRA ground vehicles now have a real ARMOUR row, built from measured metres (AMX-13 4.88 m hull, AMX-30 6.59 m, Leclerc 6.88 m, AuF1 6.70 m, AMX-10RC 6.36 m, ERC-90 5.10 m, VBL 3.87 m, VBCI 7.60 m). Four are deliberately left out: the two Pluton rows, Hades and SAMP/T, because armour3d's only missile geometry is a horizontal multi-tube MRL pack and none of those four is an MRL - they belong in tel3d.js/sam3d.js where every other faction's ballistic launcher and canister SAM already lives.

Three things drove the shape of the work:

1. The oscillating turret question. armour3d cannot express an FL-10 or FL-11: there is no two-part turret primitive. I approximated both with turret:"cast", whose lathe profile (armour3d.js:576-578) begins at 0.86 radius, undercuts to 0.96/-0.02 and only then reaches full width - that undercut below the ring is the closest thing in the builder to the gap between an oscillating turret's pivoting upper half and its fixed collar, and the AMX-13/EBR turrets really are rounded in plan. What is lost is the flat rectangular magazine bustle at the rear. I considered turret:"wedge" (box + cheek + separate bustle, which would give the bustle) and rejected it: a modern faceted wedge on a 1952 tank reads wrong at every zoom, and the wedge draws three stowage bars across the bustle top that the FL-10 does not have.

2. Where France fielded the American vehicle, the row reproduces the American vehicle. fra_e50_mbt is a straight M47 Patton (6.36 m hull, 3.51 m wide, cast turret with a deep bustle on a Pershing-pattern ww2 hull, six road wheels, five return rollers, REAR drive sprocket) - not a redressed M48, and notably not sprocketFront:true, which the existing nato_e50_mbt M48 row has wrong. fra_e90_mlrs and fra_e00_mlrs are copied field-for-field off nato_e90_mlrs because the LRM and the LRU are M270s, with only the designation and camo changed - the same move the table already makes for pla_e90_sam ("The Russian vehicle, because it is the Russian vehicle").

3. Two French signatures the builder CAN carry and that nothing else in the table has: the AMX-30 and the Leclerc both get brake:false, evac:false, so their gun tubes come out completely plain - no muzzle brake, no evacuator bulge. That is historically correct (French turret scavenging instead of a bore evacuator) and it is a genuine at-a-glance discriminator against every other 105/120 in the roster, all of which carry one bulge or the other.

Two rows use the schema in a way the table has not: fra_e60_spg (Mk F3) uses turret:"opentop" rather than the table's usual kind:"open" + turret:"none", because build() at armour3d.js:1906-1921 only calls addGun inside the turret branch or the casemate branch - a row with turret:"none" and kind:"open" renders with NO GUN AT ALL. nato_e50_spg (M44), roc_e50_spg (Priest), roc_e60_spg (M110), pla_e60_spg and kpa_e60_spg are all currently in that state and their comments describe barrels that are not drawn. And fra_e50_spg / fra_e60_spg set turretAt:-0.15 with no turret purely to flip engineDeck's `fwd` test (armour3d.js:376), which puts the engine louvres at the FRONT - correct for every AMX-13 derivative, since that chassis carries its powerpack in the nose.
design.schema_notes:
FIELD LIST, in the exact order every row in the table uses it (25 fields):
era, fac, role, designation, kind, len, width, height, hull, turret, turretAt, gunCal, gunLen, brake, evac, mantlet, track, wheels, wheelR, susp, rollers, sprocketFront, skirts, extras, camo.

HOW I VERIFIED: I grepped js/armour3d.js for every string literal compared against a P.<field> and read each branch. A value not in these lists is a SILENT no-op - the vehicle renders, wrongly, and nothing throws. I then wrote all 34 rows to a scratch file and ran a python checker over them that asserts (a) the field set and order match the table exactly, (b) every enum value is in the verified list below, (c) every extras string is one armour3d actually tests for, (d) no row has a gun that will never be drawn. All 34 passed.

--- hull (armour3d.js:137-176, `HULLS[P.hull] || HULLS.modern`) ---
RECOGNISED: "ww2" (sharp short glacis, nose beak), "modern" (one very long shallow glacis off a near-ground nose), "boxy" (upright front plate, slab sides), "boat" (pointed prow in PLAN - nose half-width 0.240).
Anything else silently falls back to "modern".
IMPORTANT: for a WHEELED row the HULLS table is never consulted at all. hull is read only at armour3d.js:1874 and 1881, where `P.hull === "boat"` is the single toggle between a pointed prow (bow 0.22-0.24, cheek 0.30-0.34) and a blunt one (bow 0.14-0.16, cheek 0.14-0.20). So on a wheeled row, hull:"boat" means "pointed prow" and nothing else - it carries no amphibious implication. I used it for the EBR-75 and the ERC-90 for exactly that reason.

--- turret (armour3d.js:573-643) ---
RECOGNISED: "cast" (lathed dome, scaled 1.24 in X, undercut below the ring, flat roof, 2 hatches), "welded" (box tl*1.7 x tw*1.9 + sloped face), "wedge" (body + angled cheek + separate rear bustle with 3 stowage bars), "small" (box tl*0.92 x tw*1.20 + small sloped face, 1 hatch), "opentop" (four walls + floor, mount at x:0 z:th*0.52), "none"/absent.
AN INVENTED VALUE IS THE WORST FAILURE IN THIS FILE: buildTurret creates the group but adds no geometry, while build() at :1907 still passes `P.turret && P.turret !== "none"`, so addGun runs against the DEFAULT mount {x: tl*0.60, z: th*0.42}. Result: a gun barrel floating in mid-air with nothing under it. I used only the six values above.

--- mantlet (armour3d.js:669-679, inside addGun) ---
RECOGNISED: "cast" (squashed sphere), "slab" (box). "none" or any other value draws nothing. Only reached when gunCal is non-zero.

--- susp (armour3d.js:419-420, 491) ---
RECOGNISED, i.e. actually changes geometry: "christie" (road wheels at FULL radius and return rollers forced to zero regardless of the rollers field) and "bogie" (road wheels at 0.78 radius). "torsion" and "none" both land in the default branch and are identical to each other. susp is read ONLY inside the tracked runningGear, so on a wheeled row it is pure documentation - the table writes "none" there and I followed that.
NOTE: the Leclerc has hydropneumatic suspension. There is no value for that, so I wrote susp:"torsion" rather than invent "hydro", which would render identically but would be a fabricated token in a table people read.

--- skirts (armour3d.js:505-519) ---
RECOGNISED: "none"/absent (nothing), "full" (one continuous plate per side). ANY other string falls into the else branch and draws the 6-segment hinged skirt - so "segmented" is real only by convention, not by test. I used exactly "none", "full", "segmented". Also gated on P.track: skirts on a wheeled row do nothing.

--- camo (armour3d.js:20-28 PAINT, 64-65 SEC) ---
RECOGNISED PAINT KEYS: olive, green, desert, sand, twotone, darkgrey, bluegrey, white. Unknown -> silently PAINT.olive.
Of those, only twotone, green, desert, darkgrey, olive have disruptive blotch tones in SEC; sand, bluegrey and white come out as a flat base with weld seams only.
I used "olive" for e50/e60/e80 (vert armee, plain, which is what the Armee de Terre ran until the 3-tone scheme arrived) and "twotone" for e90/e00.

--- kind (armour3d.js:201, 371-376, 842-847, 1915, 1928) ---
VALUES THAT DO SOMETHING: "rocket" (turretShare 0.45 instead of 0.34; engine deck forced forward; wheelBody -> truck; sent to rocketPack), "truck" (engine deck forward; wheelBody -> truck), "casemate" (engine deck window; and, ONLY when turret is none, builds the casemate superstructure and hangs a fixed gun off the hull), "apc" (wheelBody -> apc for a WHEELED row only).
VALUES THAT ARE PURE DOCUMENTATION: "tank", "wheeled", "open", "halftrack". They are never compared anywhere. I still used them, because the table does and they are the only record of what the vehicle is.

--- extras (armour3d.js:714-787, has() at :714) ---
ACTUALLY DRAWN, and requiring a turret (guarded `&& T`): cupola, irlight, aaMg, smoke, era, stowage.
ACTUALLY DRAWN on the hull, no turret needed: trimvane, fueldrums, spareTrack, slat.
SILENT NO-OPS, used widely by the existing table and therefore kept as documentation: netting, snorkel, sideMg. There is no has() branch for any of the three.
CONSEQUENCE I had to design around: on a turretless row (fra_e50_ifv, fra_e50_spg, the two mlrs rows, fra_e00_radarv) cupola/aaMg/stowage are inert. The table already does this everywhere - nato_e50_ifv, nato_e50_spg, nato_e90_mlrs all list extras that never render - so I kept them for house consistency, but I added spareTrack to the AMX-VTT and the Mk 61 so those rows have at least one extra that actually appears.
AUTOMATIC SLAT: armour3d.js:1360 bolts a slat cage onto EVERY wheeled hull of era rank >= 6 (e00/e10/e20) unless extras already contains "slat" or the role is spaag or radarv. It cannot otherwise be suppressed. So fra_e00_ifv (VBCI), fra_e00_lighttank (AMX-10RCR) and fra_e00_recon (VBL) will all wear a cage whether asked or not. On the RCR that is correct (it really was rebuilt with bar armour, and I wrote the comment around it); on the VBCI and VBL it reads as the bolted applique those vehicles carry, which I judged tolerable. fra_e00_spaag (Crotale, role spaag) and fra_e00_radarv/fra_e00_spg (truck body, armourDetail never runs) are exempt.

--- the numeric fields ---
len/width/height are real metres and len is the HULL length, not gun-forward (verified against nato_e50_mbt 6.9 for a 6.88 m M48 and pact_e60_mbt 6.6 for a 6.63 m T-62).
height is split between hull and turret: hullTopZ = max(hullBase + L*0.03, height * (1 - turretShare)) with turretShare 0.34 with a turret, 0.16 without, 0.45 for kind:"rocket" (armour3d.js:201-205); turretH is whatever is left (:539). So height must be the height to the TURRET ROOF, not over the cupola, or the turret comes out a foot too tall. I used roof heights throughout and let the cupola extra add the rest.
wheels means road wheels per side when track:true (min 3), and AXLE COUNT clamped to 2..5 when track:false (:877). wheelR is the road-wheel or tyre radius and also sets the track belt width (beltW = wheelR*1.15) and the hull ride height.
rollers is ignored entirely when susp is "christie".
turretAt is a fraction of len. It has a second, undocumented effect: at :376 a value strictly below -0.10 puts the engine deck at the FRONT of the hull. I used that deliberately on fra_e50_spg and fra_e60_spg (turretAt:-0.15, turret:"none"/"opentop") because the AMX-13 family carries its powerpack in the nose - on those two rows turretAt does nothing else at all.
gunLen is the visible barrel from the trunnion, and I solved each one backwards from the real gun-forward overall length: gunLen = (overall - len/2) - mountX, where mountX is R*1.06 for cast (R = width*0.30), tl*0.82 for welded, tl*0.86 for wedge, tl*0.50 for small and 0 for opentop, all offset by turretAt*len.
evac draws the bore-evacuator bulge at 0.62 of barrel length; brake draws the muzzle brake and its two side ports.

--- registration and the era repaint (verified) ---
registerAll() at armour3d.js:1963-1978 keys UNIT_MODELS by the ARMOUR key VERBATIM: UNIT_MODELS[key] = {len: Q.len || 6.5, build: ...}. It is invoked by the last line of armour_specs.js, and it SKIPS any id for which UNIT_MODELS already holds a non-crude entry. index.html loads armour_specs.js at line 277, before sam3d.js (290) and tel3d.js (291), both of which assign UNIT_MODELS[id] directly and therefore win - but neither registers any fra_* id, so nothing here is shadowed.
render3d.js modelKeyFor() (:309-321) returns def.id when UNIT_MODELS[def.id] exists, so the ARMOUR key MUST equal the UNITS id exactly. I confirmed all 34 ids against js/eras.js: every one of fra_e50_mbt ... fra_e00_spaag is a real unit key there, and the ids are fac_era_role exactly as in the table.
THE CONSEQUENCE THAT CHANGES WHAT YOU WRITE IN A ROW: getModel() at render3d.js:437 computes K = (ERA_KIT[era] && key !== def.id) ? ERA_KIT[era] : null. The moment a French vehicle has its OWN row, key === def.id and K is null - so eraPaint() and eraKitFor() stop running on it. Today these units borrow an American mesh and get a free period tint plus a bolt-on searchlight/stowage-basket/slat-cage. After these rows land they get neither. The period has to come entirely out of the row's own camo and extras, which is why I put irlight explicitly on both AMX-30 rows and smoke on the B2, rather than leaving the era kit to supply them.

rows.comment: /* The American tank unchanged, because that is what France was given: a long cast turret with a deep bustle over a Pershing-pattern hull with a nose beak, six road wheels under five return rollers and the drive sprocket at the tail. */
rows.row: fra_e50_mbt: {era:"e50", fac:"fra", role:"mbt", designation:"M47 Patton (MDAP deliveries to the Armee de Terre)", kind:"tank", len:6.36, width:3.51, height:3, hull:"ww2", turret:"cast", turretAt:0.02, gunCal:90, gunLen:4.2, brake:true, evac:true, mantlet:"cast", track:true, wheels:6, wheelR:0.33, susp:"torsion", rollers:5, sprocketFront:false, skirts:"none", extras:["cupola","aaMg","stowage","spareTrack"], camo:"olive"},
rows.designation: M47 Patton (MDAP deliveries to the Armee de Terre)

rows.comment: /* Tiny five-wheel hull with the drive sprocket at the nose and the turret shoved right to the tail, a muzzle-braked 75mm reaching a metre and a half past the bow; the oscillating FL-10 is approximated by a cast turret whose undercut below the ring reads as the pivot gap. */
rows.row: fra_e50_lighttank: {era:"e50", fac:"fra", role:"lighttank", designation:"AMX-13 Modele 51 with the FL-10 oscillating turret", kind:"tank", len:4.88, width:2.51, height:2.3, hull:"ww2", turret:"cast", turretAt:-0.12, gunCal:75, gunLen:3.7, brake:true, evac:false, mantlet:"none", track:true, wheels:5, wheelR:0.3, susp:"torsion", rollers:3, sprocketFront:true, skirts:"none", extras:["cupola","stowage","aaMg"], camo:"olive"},
rows.designation: AMX-13 Modele 51 with the FL-10 oscillating turret

rows.comment: /* A lengthened AMX-13 chassis with the turret taken off: a plain slab-sided tracked box, front drive sprockets under five small road wheels, and an open ring mount where the commander stands. */
rows.row: fra_e50_ifv: {era:"e50", fac:"fra", role:"ifv", designation:"AMX-VTT Modele 56 (Vehicule Transport de Troupe)", kind:"apc", len:5.7, width:2.67, height:2.4, hull:"boxy", turret:"none", turretAt:0, gunCal:0, gunLen:0, brake:false, evac:false, mantlet:"none", track:true, wheels:5, wheelR:0.3, susp:"torsion", rollers:3, sprocketFront:true, skirts:"none", extras:["aaMg","stowage","spareTrack"], camo:"olive"},

rows.comment: /* Eight wheels under a long pointed hull that is the same shape at both ends, because it has a driver at both ends; the two retracting steel centre pairs are drawn as ordinary tyres and the oscillating FL-11 as a small cast turret. */
rows.row: fra_e50_recon: {era:"e50", fac:"fra", role:"recon", designation:"Panhard EBR-75 Modele 1951, tourelle FL-11", kind:"wheeled", len:5.56, width:2.42, height:2.24, hull:"boat", turret:"cast", turretAt:0, gunCal:75, gunLen:2.6, brake:true, evac:false, mantlet:"none", track:false, wheels:4, wheelR:0.5, susp:"none", rollers:0, sprocketFront:false, skirts:"none", extras:["cupola","stowage"], camo:"olive"},

rows.comment: /* No turret at all: a tall fixed box superstructure filling the back of a stubby AMX-13 chassis, with the short 105 poking forward over a front engine deck and a front drive sprocket. */

rows.comment: /* Very low five-wheel hull under a long rounded cast turret, and a 105 that is a completely plain tube - no muzzle brake and no bore evacuator bulge anywhere along it, which nothing else in the roster can say. */

uncovered: fra_e60_tel (Pluton, missile nucleaire tactique sur chassis AMX-30) - NOT WRITTEN. The whole silhouette is a single 7.6 m boxed missile on an elevating ramp over an AMX-30 hull. armour3d's only missile geometry is rocketPack (armour3d.js:1800-1862), which draws a rectangular honeycomb of tubes whose rows and columns come from the era rank alone - 2 rows x 8 columns at e60, 4 x 5 from e80 on. A Pluton rendered through it becomes a sixteen-tube Katyusha rail frame on a tank hull, which is worse than the borrowed launcher it currently falls back to. Expressing it as turret:"welded" with gunCal 0 gives a 3.4 m box where a 7.6 m container should be, because the welded turret is sized at tl*1.7 off the hull length and cannot be stretched. This belongs in js/tel3d.js beside nato_e60_tel and pact_e60_tel, which is exactly what the header comment at the top of the sam/tel block in armour_specs.js says.

fra_e80_tel (Pluton, on the AMX-30 chassis) - NOT WRITTEN, same reason, and worse: at era rank 4 rocketPack switches to 4 rows of 5, so the single nuclear round would come out as a twenty-tube MRL block.

fra_e90_tel (Hades short-range nuclear missile system) - NOT WRITTEN. Hades is not a self-propelled vehicle at all: it is a two-round erector semitrailer towed by a Renault tractor. The spec table has no tractor-and-trailer primitive (nato_e80_sam fakes the Patriot M901 with a single 15.4 m boxy row and the comment admits it is 'a tractor and a semitrailer, not one vehicle'). I could have copied that dodge, but a 15 m truck row for Hades would be a guess about a vehicle I cannot check, and it would still draw a tube honeycomb rather than two missiles on an erector beam.

fra_e00_sam (SAMP/T with Aster 30 Block 1) - NOT WRITTEN. The SAMP/T launcher is eight Aster canisters standing VERTICALLY on an 8x8. Every piece of missile geometry in armour3d lies horizontally along +X: rocketPack's tubes are cylinders rotated onto the X axis and then pitched by a fixed 0.10 rad. There is no vertical-launch primitive and no way to fake one from the fields in this table, so the honest answer is a hand-authored builder in js/sam3d.js alongside nato_e00_sam and pact_e00_sam rather than a row here.

reviews.reasoning:
I read js/armour3d.js (1989 lines) in full and built an independent inventory of every field the builder reads and every value it tests, then machine-checked all 34 rows.

THE SCHEMA LAYER IS CLEAN. I could not break it.

- Fields read by the builder: grep of `P.<name>` yields exactly brake, camo, era, evac, extras, gunCal, gunLen, height, hull, kind, len, mantlet, role, rollers, skirts, sprocketFront, susp, track, turret, turretAt, wheelR, wheels, width. `fac` and `designation` are inert but are in all 258 existing rows. No row in the plan uses a field name outside that set.
- Enum values: hull {ww2, modern, boxy, boat} (armour3d.js:178 `HULLS[P.hull] || HULLS.modern`); turret {cast:573, welded:591, wedge:602, small:621, opentop:631, none}; mantlet {cast:669, slab:674}; camo the 8 PAINT keys at :20-28; extras with a has() branch = cupola/irlight/aaMg/smoke/era/stowage/trimvane/fueldrums/spareTrack/slat (:714-787). A python pass over all 34 rows found ZERO unrecognised values in hull, turret, mantlet, camo, era, and zero unknown extras strings other than "netting", which the plan itself labels a documented no-op and which nato_e00_radarv already carries verbatim.
- Field order: all 34 rows use the same 25 fields in the same order as every existing row (checked against nato_e60_sam and 257 others).
- Ids: all 34 are real UNITS keys in js/eras.js, cat "vehicle", layer "ground", and every `role` and `designation` string matches the unit's own role and "full" field character for character. The "38 FRA ground vehicles" arithmetic is right: fra_e90_sam is NOT a key (eras.js:10454 is a comment saying it "is DROPPED"), so 39 grep hits minus that = 38 = 34 written + 4 uncovered.
- Registration: no fra_* id exists anywhere in UNIT_MODELS before armour_specs.js runs (grep -rl "fra_e" js/ hits only rules.js, generations.js, eras.js); sam3d.js and tel3d.js register no fra ids (every "fra" hit in both files is the word "frame"); index.html loads armour3d 276, armour_specs 277, sam3d 290, tel3d 291 exactly as the plan states; armour_specs.js's last line calls Armour3D.registerAll(). Nothing is shadowed and nothing is skipped.
- Spot-checked claims that turned out true: mountX formulas (I re-derived gun-forward overall lengths of 9.48 m AMX-30, 9.92 m Leclerc, 6.35 m AMX-13, 7.70 m ERC-90, 9.13 m AMX-10RC, 6.15 m EBR-75 — all within centimetres of reality); the "gun never drawn" list (my own scan found exactly nato_e50_spg, roc_e50_spg, kpa_e60_spg, pla_e60_spg, roc_e60_spg — plus a sixth the plan missed, roc_e90_ifv); the automatic slat rule at :1360 and which fra rows it catches; turretAt < -0.10 flipping engineDeck at :376.

WHERE IT BREAKS: exactly one row, fra_e00_spg (CAESAR), and it breaks because it does something no row in the table's 258-row history has ever done — put a turret on a truck body. I scanned all 258 rows: zero truck-body rows (kind truck/rocket, or role supply/radarv/mlrs/ewveh) carry a turret. build():1911-1912 has a special case for it, but the arithmetic puts the 7.4 m barrel straight through the cab. Three lesser issues follow. All are salvageable, so SOUND_WITH_FIXES rather than BROKEN.

fatals.which: fra_e00_spg (CAESAR) — the 155 mm barrel is drawn through the truck cab
fatals.problem: This is the FIRST row in the table's history to give a truck body a turret — I scanned all 258 existing rows and every kind:"truck"/kind:"rocket"/role supply|radarv|mlrs|ewveh row has turret:"none". The builder handles it, but the arithmetic collides. build() at armour3d.js:1911-1912 pins the turret to the bed floor, not to the vehicle height: `var tz = hullTopZ(P, L); if (F && F.bed) tz = F.bed.bedZ;`. For a truck, hullTopZ is the bed, not the roof — wheelFrame at armour3d.js:912 ends the truck branch with `F.top = F.bedZ;`. With len 10, wheelR 0.6: railZ = 0.93, bedZ = max(1.074, 1.17) = 1.17, and truckBody returns B.bedZ = 1.17 + t*1.3 = 1.352 (t = L*0.014 = 0.14). turretH = max(L*0.045, height - hullTopZ) = 3 - 1.17 = 1.83. The opentop mount is `mount = { x: 0, z: th * 0.52 };` (armour3d.js:643), so the trunnion lands at z = 1.352 + 0.952 = 2.30, and addGun lays a horizontal cylinder of radius max(L*0.010, 0.155*0.55) = 0.10 from x = turretAt*L = -2.2 forward 7.4 m to x = +5.2. Meanwhile the cab is a solid body from x = cabB 3.05 to cabF 5.0 (armour3d.js:911-912), floor at bedZ 1.17, roof at F.roof = bedZ + cabH = 1.17 + 1.55 = 2.72, with the side glass and windscreen spanning z 1.852 to 2.58. The barrel at z 2.20–2.40 crosses that band over the whole 1.95 m of cab. The CAESAR renders with its gun tube skewering the driver's windscreen. No value of turretAt fixes it — the barrel is horizontal and the cab is ahead of every legal mount — and no value of gunLen short enough to stop at x=3.05 (≤5.25 m) leaves any muzzle overhang at all.
fatals.correction: Raise `height` from 3 to 4.2. For a truck row, `height` feeds ONLY turretH — bedZ, cabH and cabOver are all independent of it once height ≥ 2.72 (cabH = max(0.92, min(1.55, h - bedZ)) saturates at 1.55) — so this lifts the trunnion and nothing else. At h = 4.2: th = 3.03, mount z = 1.576, gun centre z = 2.93, barrel underside 2.83, clearing the 2.72 cab roof by 11 cm. The threshold is h > 3.993, so do not use 3.7 or 4.0. Accept that the opentop tub walls grow to th*0.78 = 2.36 m, which reads as the gun's cradle/shield tower behind the cab. If that tower is unacceptable, the alternative is to drop kind:"truck" for kind:"wheeled" — wheelBody() at armour3d.js:850 then returns "apc" (ax 3, L 10) and builds an armoured monocoque with NO cab at all, roof at 2.22, gun at 2.63 — but you lose the lorry cab that is the CAESAR's whole identity.

fatals.which: fra_e50_spg — the turretAt:-0.15 "engine louvres at the FRONT" trick is invisible on this row
fatals.problem: The plan's summary says fra_e50_spg and fra_e60_spg both set turretAt:-0.15 "purely to flip engineDeck's `fwd` test (armour3d.js:376), which puts the engine louvres at the FRONT". The flip happens on both rows, but on fra_e50_spg the result is buried. With kind:"casemate", engineDeck takes the `else if (P.kind === "casemate") { obsR = -L * 0.26; obsF = L * 0.30; }` branch at armour3d.js:371, so fwd gives x0 = max(L*0.08, L*0.30) = 0.30L and x1 = min(F.frontX - L*0.025, x0 + L*0.30); for the ww2 table F.frontX = 0.30L, so x1 = 0.275L < x0 and the `if (x1 - x0 < L * 0.08) x0 = x1 - L * 0.08;` guard rewinds it to 0.195L..0.275L — a panel 0.08L long sitting at z = top + t*0.5 = top + 0.04, half-width hw*1.70/2 = 1.115. casemate() at armour3d.js:846-848 then draws `new THREE.BoxGeometry(L * 0.50, W * 0.88, h)` at `(L * 0.02, 0, top + h * 0.42)` with h = L*0.090 = 0.513 — i.e. x from -0.23L to +0.27L, half-width 1.166, z from top-0.041 to top+0.472. The engine panel, its six louvre bars and both exhaust cowls are entirely inside that box. Nothing of the forward engine deck is visible. (kpa_e50_spg and pla_e50_spg already sit in the same state, so this is house behaviour, not a regression — but the plan's stated rationale for the value does not hold on this row.)
fatals.correction: Keep turretAt:-0.15 if you want (it is harmless), but delete the claim that it puts louvres at the front of the Mk 61 — on a casemate row it does nothing visible. If you want a visibly nose-engined AMX-13 derivative, only fra_e60_spg (turret:"opentop", no casemate box) actually delivers it: there the deck lands at 0.12L..0.275L and the tub sits at -1.69..-0.02, so the louvres are in clear air ahead of the mount.

fatals.which: fra_e50_mbt, fra_e50_spg, fra_e60_mbt — `spareTrack` is drawn floating in mid-air off the bow
fatals.problem: The plan says it added spareTrack "to the AMX-VTT and the Mk 61 so those rows have at least one extra that actually appears". It appears, but not on the hull. addExtras places it unconditionally at `st.position.set(L * 0.36, 0, top + L * 0.010);` (armour3d.js:783), where top = hullTopZ. The deck plate only runs out to F.frontX, which hullFrame derives from the HULLS table: 0.30L for "ww2" and 0.15L for "modern". So on any ww2- or modern-hulled row the block is placed forward of the deck edge, over the glacis, at full roof height. For fra_e60_mbt (modern, len 6.59): deck ends at x 0.99, the block sits at x 2.37, z 1.584, while the lofted glacis surface at that station is z 1.08 — the spare track link hangs 0.50 m above the plate and 1.38 m ahead of the deck. For fra_e50_spg (ww2, len 5.7) it floats ~0.33 m clear. Only fra_e50_ifv gets it right, because "boxy" carries the deck out to 0.39L > 0.36L. (pact_e50_spg, kpa_e80_spg and roc_e90_lighttank already do this, so it is a pre-existing builder fault, not something these rows invent.)
fatals.correction: Drop "spareTrack" from fra_e50_mbt (hull ww2), fra_e50_spg (hull ww2) and fra_e60_mbt (hull modern), or accept a known floating artefact. It is correct as written only on fra_e50_ifv, whose hull:"boxy" carries the deck plate past x = 0.36L. Substitute "fueldrums" (armour3d.js:774, placed at -L*0.44, well inside the tail) if those rows need a hull-mounted extra that renders.

fatals.which: fra_e90_mbt/fra_e00_mbt, fra_e90_mlrs/fra_e00_mlrs, fra_e60_spaag/fra_e80_spaag — three pairs render byte-identically
fatals.problem: In each pair every field the builder reads is the same, and `era` itself changes nothing on a tracked row: eraR() is consumed only by rocketPack's rows/cols split (`er <= 2 ? 2 : 4` — e90 rank 5 and e00 rank 6 both give 4x5), by wheelFrame's tyre width, by seam(), and by the wheeled slat rule at armour3d.js:1360. None of those is reached by a tracked row. So Leclerc s1 and Leclerc s2, the LRM and the LRU, and the two AMX-13 DCA rows produce identical meshes — and because each now has its own ARMOUR key, render3d.js:437 sets `K = (ERA_KIT[era] && key !== def.id) ? ERA_KIT[era] : null` to null, so the era repaint that used to separate them is gone too. The plan correctly identifies this ERA_KIT consequence in its schema notes but does not connect it to the three collided pairs. The LRM/LRU and the two DCA rows are genuinely the same vehicle, so those are defensible; the Leclerc pair is not, since S2/SXXI is the visibly different one.
fatals.correction: Give fra_e00_mbt at least one rendering-relevant difference from fra_e90_mbt. The cheapest honest one inside the schema: add "era" to fra_e00_mbt's extras (armour3d.js:743 draws a 3x3 applique brick pattern on the turret front, and the S2's turret front really is a different armour block), or switch fra_e00_mbt's camo to "darkgrey"/"green" — both have SEC blotch tones at armour3d.js:64-65, so both visibly differ from "twotone". Leave the mlrs and spaag pairs as they are and say in the comment that they are the same vehicle.

reviews.reasoning:
I read js/armour3d.js end-to-end (HULLS 137-176, hullTopZ 195-205, engineDeck 361-400, runningGear 405-495, addSkirts 505-519, buildTurret 573-651, addGun 659-705, addExtras 710-787, casemate 790-807, wheelBody 840-850, wheelFrame 875-920, the auto-slat at 1360, rocketPack 1798-1862, build 1893-1960, registerAll 1963-1978), js/armour_specs.js (258 existing rows, no fra_* row exists yet, field order confirmed against nato_e50_mbt), js/render3d.js (modelKeyFor 309-321, getModel 437-441), index.html load order, and the 38 FRA ground unit entries in js/eras.js.

WHAT SURVIVES THE ATTACK. I could not break the schema claims. I machine-checked all 34 rows: field set and order match the table exactly (25 fields), every enum value is one the builder actually tests (hull/turret/mantlet/susp/skirts/camo/kind), every extras string is either a real has() branch or one of the three documented no-ops the table already uses, and all 34 ids are real keys in eras.js with from/to matching the row's era. Every designation string is character-for-character the unit's own "full" field in eras.js, so no era assignment is invented here. No fra_* id appears in sam3d.js, tel3d.js or models3d*.js, so nothing shadows the registration, and registerAll() is invoked on the last line of armour_specs.js. The code claims are all true: addGun is called at only two sites (1909 turret, 1920 casemate), so kind:"open"+turret:"none" really does render gunless; turretAt < -0.10 really does flip engineDeck's fwd; susp:"christie" really does zero rollers; rocketPack really is 2x8 tubes at e60 and 4x5 from e80.

The vehicle facts are mostly excellent and independently reproduce. I recomputed each row's gun-forward overall length through the builder's own mount arithmetic (cast R*1.06 with R=W*0.30; welded tl*0.82, wedge tl*0.86, small tl*0.50, opentop 0, all at tl=L*0.30, offset by turretAt*len, plus len/2): EBR 6.15 vs real 6.15, AML-90 5.14 vs 5.11, ERC-90 7.70 vs 7.69, AMX-10RC 9.13 vs 9.15, AMX-30 9.48 vs 9.48, Leclerc 9.92 vs 9.87, AuF1 10.36 vs 10.25, M47 8.62 vs 8.51, AMX-13/75 6.35 vs 6.36. Hull dimensions check out against the real vehicles (AMX-13 4.88/2.51/2.30, AMX-VCI 5.70/2.67/2.41, AMX-30 6.59/3.10, AMX-10P 5.78/2.78/2.57, AML 3.79/1.97, ERC 5.10/2.50/2.25, AMX-10RC 6.36/2.95/2.68, AuF1 6.70/3.15/3.25, Leclerc 6.88/3.71/2.53, VAB 5.98/2.49, VBL 3.87/2.02, VBCI 7.60/2.98/3.00, M270 6.9/3.0/2.6). Wheel counts and drive ends are right: M47 six road wheels, five return rollers, REAR sprocket (and the plan is correct that the existing nato_e50_mbt M48 row has sprocketFront:true wrong - the M48 is rear-drive too); AMX-13 family five wheels, FRONT sprocket; AMX-30 five wheels, five return rollers, rear sprocket; AML 2 axles = 4x4; EBR 4 axles = 8x8; ERC/AMX-10RC 3 axles = 6x6; VBCI 4 axles = 8x8. brake:false + evac:false on the AMX-30's CN-105-F1 and the Leclerc's 120/52 is historically right (French bore scavenging, no evacuator, no muzzle brake) and is a genuine discriminator. The turret choices are defensible: no invented value, no gun floating on an empty group.

WHAT BREAKS. Three rows have concrete numeric defects and one class of comment is wrong.

(1) fra_e00_spg CAESAR is the worst row. len:10 is the gun-forward travel length, which violates the table's own stated rule that len is the HULL length - the Sherpa 6x6 body is about 8 m - so the lorry itself is drawn 2 m too long and then a 7.4 m tube is added on top of that. Worse, this is the first row in the file to put a gun on kind:"truck" (I grepped: every existing truck row has gunCal 0), and the configuration does not work. With height:3.0 the builder computes F.bedZ 1.17, B.bedZ 1.35, turretH = 3.0-1.17 = 1.83, opentop mount z = th*0.52, so the barrel is drawn horizontally at z 2.30 while the cab body occupies z 1.17-2.72 over x 3.05-5.00. The tube passes through the cab and out of the windscreen.

(2) fra_e50_spg Mk 61 gets the casemate mount wrong. The plan's gunLen formula lists mount offsets for the five turret kinds but the casemate path is different: build() at :1920 calls addGun with NO mx, so x0 falls back to L*0.14 inside a group already positioned at cm.x = L*0.24 - an effective trunnion at L*0.38. With gunLen 2.2 the muzzle lands 1.52 m past the bow, making a vehicle whose real overall length equals its 5.70 m hull come out 7.22 m long, with the mantlet slab floating detached ahead of the casemate face (which is at L*0.27).

(3) fra_e60_spg Mk F3 is 0.87 m too long by the plan's own method: mount at turretAt*len = -0.855, gunLen 5.1 gives 7.09 m overall against the real 6.22 m.

(4) Four rows carry comments describing geometry that will not exist. gunCal:0 makes addGun return immediately, so the Roland rows (fra_e80_sam, fra_e90_spaag), the Crotale row and the VAB Mephisto row render as a bare box or an empty tub - no launch tubes, no missile boxes, no radar dish. This is exactly the failure the plan condemns in nato_e50_spg/roc_e60_spg ("their comments describe barrels that are not drawn"), committed four times.

(5) Engine deck at the wrong end on five front-engined French chassis. The plan establishes that the AMX-13 family carries its powerpack in the nose and uses turretAt < -0.10 to move the louvres forward - then does not apply it to the AMX-VTT (turretAt 0), the two AMX-13 DCA rows (-0.05) or the three AMX-10P rows (0), all of which are front-engined. Those five render with the louvres and exhaust cowls at the tail.

None of this renders the wrong VEHICLE CLASS and nothing is a silent no-op the builder ignores, so this is not BROKEN; it is three numbers, five turretAt values and four comments away from correct.

fatals.problem: Two defects in one row. (a) len:10 is the gun-forward travel length, not the hull length - the row's own schema_notes says "len is the HULL length, not gun-forward" - so the lorry body is drawn ~2 m too long and the wheelbase stretched with it. (b) This is the first kind:"truck" row in the file to carry a gun (every existing truck row has gunCal 0) and the arrangement does not work: wheelFrame gives F.bedZ 1.17 and truckBody returns B.bedZ 1.35; hullTopZ for a truck is F.bedZ, so turretH = 3.0 - 1.17 = 1.83 and the opentop mount sits at th*0.52 = 0.95 above the bed, putting the barrel horizontally at z 2.30. The cab body spans z 1.17-2.72 over x 3.05-5.00 and the 7.4 m tube ends at x 5.2, so the barrel is drawn straight through the cab and out of the windscreen.
fatals.correction: len:8.0 (the Sherpa 6x6 chassis; the quoted 10 m is with the barrel over the cab), gunLen:7.8 (keeps the muzzle ~2 m past the bumper, i.e. 10.0 m overall), and height:3.9 instead of 3.0 - the real CAESAR travel height is 3.7 m and at 3.9 the trunnion computes to z 2.74, just clearing the 2.72 m cab roof instead of passing through it. If the tall open tub that follows from height:3.9 is unacceptable, the CAESAR belongs with the four rows the plan already deferred to a hand-authored builder.

fatals.which: fra_e50_spg (Obusier de 105 mm Mle 50 / Mk 61, casemate)
fatals.problem: The gunLen was solved with the wrong mount offset. The plan's formula lists mountX for cast/welded/wedge/small/opentop but the casemate path is none of those: build() at armour3d.js:1920 calls addGun(THREE, fake, P, L, W) with no mx, so x0 defaults to L*0.14 INSIDE a group already positioned at cm.x = L*0.24 (casemate() returns {x: L*0.24}). Effective trunnion = L*0.38 = 2.17 m. With gunLen 2.2 the muzzle ends 1.52 m past the bow, so a vehicle whose real overall length IS its 5.70 m hull (the Mk 61's howitzer barely reaches the glacis edge) renders 7.22 m long and reads as an SU-100. The mantlet:"slab" block also lands at x 2.17, i.e. 0.63 m in front of the casemate face at L*0.27, so it floats detached over the glacis.
fatals.correction: gunLen:0.8 (muzzle at x 2.97, essentially flush with the 2.85 m bow, which is the Mk 61's real silhouette). If a visible stub is wanted, 0.9 is the ceiling. Do not copy the 2.2 used by the SU-76M rows - those rows have the same overshoot.

fatals.which: fra_e60_spg (Canon de 155 mm Mk F3 sur chassis AMX-13)
fatals.problem: gunLen:5.1 is the tube length, not the value the plan's own formula produces. With the opentop mount at turretAt*len = -0.855 the muzzle reaches x 4.245 against a bow at 2.85, i.e. 1.39 m of overhang and 7.09 m overall, against the Mk F3's real quoted 6.22 m - 0.87 m too long. The comment ("the tube lying the whole length of the hull and a metre past it") documents the error rather than the vehicle.
fatals.correction: gunLen:4.2, which gives (6.22 - 2.85) + 0.855 = 4.23 by the plan's own method and puts the muzzle ~0.5 m past the bow.

fatals.which: fra_e80_sam and fra_e90_spaag (Roland 2), fra_e00_spaag (Crotale NG), fra_e80_tankdestroyer (VAB Mephisto) - the comments
fatals.problem: All four rows have gunCal:0, and addGun returns on its first line when gunCal is falsy, so nothing is drawn on the turret at all. The Roland rows render as an empty welded box, the Crotale as an empty welded box on a 6x6 APC hull, the Mephisto as an empty opentop tub. Their comments promise geometry the builder cannot produce: "one launch tube stands on each flank and the search radar folds down between them", "four missile boxes stacked on each flank and the tracking dish between them", "a four-round missile box that rises out of the roof behind the cab". This is precisely the defect the plan indicts in nato_e50_spg, roc_e50_spg, roc_e60_spg, pla_e60_spg and kpa_e60_spg - comments describing weapons that are never drawn - reproduced four times in the new rows.
fatals.correction: Rewrite the four comments to describe what actually renders (a flat-topped box turret with no gun of any kind on an AMX-30 hull; a box module on a 6x6; a raised open tub on the VAB roof) and say in the comment that the missiles are not expressible in this table. For the Mephisto specifically, turret:"welded" would at least read as the raised armoured launcher box, which is that vehicle's whole identity, where the opentop tub reads as an open ring mount it does not have.

fatals.which: fra_e50_ifv (AMX-VTT), fra_e60_spaag and fra_e80_spaag (AMX-13 DCA), fra_e60/e80/e90_ifv (AMX-10P) - engine deck at the wrong end
fatals.problem: engineDeck() at armour3d.js:376 puts the louvres and exhaust cowls forward only when kind is rocket/truck or turretAt < -0.10. The plan states the rule correctly ("correct for every AMX-13 derivative, since that chassis carries its powerpack in the nose") and then applies it only to fra_e50_spg and fra_e60_spg. The AMX-VTT (turretAt 0), both AMX-13 DCA rows (-0.05) and all three AMX-10P rows (0) are equally front-engined - AMX-10P has the engine front-left beside the driver - so all five render with the engine deck, louvres and exhausts at the tail, on the same chassis whose siblings have them at the nose.
fatals.correction: fra_e50_ifv: turretAt:-0.15 - it has turret:"none" and kind:"apc", so turretAt does nothing else and the fix is free. fra_e60_spaag and fra_e80_spaag: turretAt:-0.12, which is doubly right because the DCA's turret really does sit at the rear of the hull. For the three AMX-10P rows it is a trade-off (turretAt:-0.12 moves the 20mm turret 0.69 m aft of centre on a 5.78 m hull); pick one and say in the comment which end of the vehicle you chose to get right.

fatals.problem: Lower confidence than the items above, but worth checking before it lands: the 75 mm SA 49 in the FL-11 turret is a plain slender tube. The muzzle brake is the signature of the SA 50 in the AMX-13's FL-10 (which the plan has right) and of the later 90 mm F1 turret; putting one on the EBR-75 hands two different French 75s the same muzzle and removes the one at-a-glance difference between the EBR and the AMX-13 in the same era.
fatals.correction: brake:false on fra_e50_recon; leave the computed 6.15 m overall alone, which already matches the real vehicle exactly. Related minor: the AMX-13 family rows use rollers:3 where the chassis carries 2 return rollers - near-invisible at RTS zoom, but rollers:2 is the correct number if the rest of the family table is being written from measurements.
